title: A transverse nonzero Fourier mode extends the neutral periodic harmonic-electric family

transverse_periodic_family.geometry: On T^3 choose nonzero lattice k perpendicular to the rotating two-plane of a(t)=A(cos(Omega t),sin(Omega t),0).
transverse_periodic_family.solution: Set phi_+(t,x)=phi_-(t,x)=R exp(i omega t) exp(i k dot x), Omega=sqrt(2)eR and omega=sqrt(m^2+|k|^2+e^2A^2).
transverse_periodic_family.scalar_equations: Because k dot a(t)=0, both charged covariant frequencies equal the constant m^2+|k|^2+e^2A^2, so both scalar equations hold exactly.
transverse_periodic_family.maxwell_and_gauss: Opposite Gauss densities cancel. The momentum current parts cancel between charges while the a-parts add to -2e^2R^2a, giving a''+2e^2R^2a=0.
transverse_periodic_family.normal_form_control: Equal same-k amplitudes give D=0 and constant M=2R^2, so both K1598's E_0 and K1593's adapted energy are constant while |E_bar|=A Omega>0.
transverse_periodic_family.route_consequence: The holonomy total variation diverges linearly although no homogeneous matter mode is present. Excluding only k=0 is insufficient; dispersion must exclude or control the full nondispersive transverse single-mode sector.
transverse_periodic_family.scope_guard: This family does not exclude scattering under stronger localization, spectral, nonresonance or radiation hypotheses, and it does not disprove a cancellation-based positive-radius theorem.
